title: Mitigating Prompt Injection via Dual-LLM Control Flow
explanation: Prompt injection remains a critical vulnerability where malicious user input hijacks language model execution by overriding system instructions. To mitigate this risk, modern architectures employ a dual-LLM control flow pattern. The primary execution model handles user requests in an isolated context without direct system authority. A secondary, privileged guardrail model analyzes incoming payloads and execution outputs against strict structural invariants before downstream execution. By completely decoupling intent classification and data ingestion from execution logic, applications prevent indirect prompt manipulation while maintaining high throughput for autonomous agent workflows.
takeaway: De-couple untrusted data ingestion from execution authority using a secondary validation model to reliably neutralize prompt injection vectors in autonomous agent architectures.
